transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-12-07 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Carlos Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Anders (Product); Dana Brooks (Aurea Labs - ML Platform Lead), Imran Shah (Principal ML Engineer), Sofia Martinez (SRE)

Summary:
Quick Optimize console walkthrough focused on comparing INT8 vs FP8 profiles, showing latency/quality delta charts, and demoing adaptive fidelity thresholds + fallback rules. Customer is concerned about clinical accuracy, worst-case regressions, and VPC/on-prem options. Agreed next steps include sandbox access, fidelity sweep, and pilot kickoff.

Topics:
- INT8 vs FP8 practical differences
- Console-driven precision profiles and thresholding
- Fallback and rollback policies (adaptive fidelity)
- Latency vs quality tradeoff charts and SLO budgeting
- Network/VPC and security checkpoints

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Carlos (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Carlos, AE on the Optimize team. Priya and Tom from our side, and we have Dana, Imran, and Sofia from Aurea. how's everyone doing?

[00:00:18] Dana (Aurea): Doing well, thanks. excited to see the console. we want to understand the int8 vs f-p eight — sorry if I say that wrong — tradeoffs for our clinical qna workload.

[00:00:34] Priya (Redwood SE): totally fine, lots of people say F-P eight. We'll show both. quick agenda: run through the Optimize console, show an INT8 profile and FP8 profile side-by-side, overlay quality metrics, then demo adaptive fidelity thresholds and a fallback runbook.

[00:00:52] Tom (Redwood Product): also want to point out cost math and how the batching/k-v cache interacts with precision profiles — that often changes numbers more than the raw bitwidth.

[00:01:10] Imran (Aurea): great. baseline: we run mostly clinical summarization and entity extraction, typical prompt lengths around 220 tokens, tail latencies matter to our triage flow. Our current SLO is p95 400ms.

[00:01:30] Sofia (Aurea SRE): security is big for us. we need to confirm VPC peering, KMS integration, SOC2 paperwork, and audit logs retention.

[00:01:46] Carlos: noted — we'll share the SOC2 and KMS integration docs after. ok jumping into the console — screen share now.

[00:02:10] [screen share noise / clicking]

[00:02:22] Priya: at the top left is the model profile selector. i'm loading a benchmark run we recently executed with your prompt set. here's INT8 profile (left) vs FP8 profile (right). look at the latency histogram — INT8 median is about 0.22s lower, p95 sits around 380ms; FP8 p95 is 270ms — sorry, i misspoke, FP8 is lower latency in this particular kernel build due to better vectorization on Ampere-based hardware — occasionally the kernel math favors FP8 on modern chips.

[00:03:05] Dana: wait that's surprising — we assumed INT8 always faster. can you explain?

[00:03:12] Priya: yep, common misconception. INT8 reduces compute but can increase memory pressure for certain kernel paths or require more emulation, depending on the attention implementation. FP8 here hits optimized kernels with lower memory copy overhead. the console shows per-kernel selection heuristics — you can see it auto-selected fp8-optimized kernels for our sequence length profile.

[00:03:40] Imran: ok that nuance matters. what about quality — how much do answers diverge?

[00:03:46] Priya: we ran an nLG and n-class accuracy sweep. quality delta chart — on the right — shows BLEU/ROUGE-like numbers and a clinical entity F1. INT8 dropped entity F1 by about 1.6 points vs FP8 on average; worst-case prompts saw up to 4 points. most single-turn summarizations stayed within our acceptable error band for exploratory flows, but for diagnostic text we recommend FP8 or an adaptive profile.

[00:04:20] Tom: that's where adaptive fidelity thresholds come in — you can set a threshold on confidence/quality metric or on prompt tags. if a prompt is high-risk (we saw you tag 'diagnosis' prompts), the system routes to FP8 or even to a full precision variant; everything else can be INT8 to save cost.

[00:04:40] Dana: how do you compute confidence? we have privacy constraints so we can't send lots of telemetry back.

[00:04:46] Priya: good question. confidence is computed locally in the inference path — a small post-token scoring pass and a lightweight heuristic we call 'fidelity-signal'. nothing leaves your VPC unless you opt-in. the signal is a scalar we expose in trace logs, and the adaptive policy uses it to decide fallback.

[00:05:05] Sofia: and the fallback — is it synchronous? does it double cost and latency?

[00:05:10] Priya: by default adaptive fallback is synchronous but optimized — we first try INT8 with KV-cache warm; if the fidelity-signal is below threshold, we do one of two options: quick re-roll on FP8 with a warm KV (fast path), or async re-score with human-in-loop. the console shows expected cost deltas for both. re-roll FP8 for failed cases adds about 20-35% compute for those requests but keeps the overall unit cost down because most traffic stays INT8.

[00:05:45] Imran: demonstrate the fallback live?

[00:05:48] Priya: sure — i'm going to trigger a high-risk prompt tagged 'diagnosis' and show the runbook.

[00:06:02] [typing sound]

[00:06:10] Priya: okay request sent. you can see on the trace pane: step 1 INT8 exec, fidelity-signal 0.62 (below the 0.7 threshold), policy fired, re-routed to FP8 with warm KV, final answer generated. timeline shows extra 110ms for re-roll, still within a p95 of 450ms for these cases — configurable.

[00:06:40] Dana: that 110ms is acceptable if quality improves. can you show an example of a failure mode where INT8 regresses significantly?

[00:06:48] Priya: pulling a worst-case from the sweep. here's a prompt about nuanced medication interactions — INT8 omitted a contraindication, FP8 included it. you can see token-level diffs in the console; there's also an auto-generated delta score.

[00:07:15] Imran: the token diff UI is nice. can we export these deltas to our eval pipeline?

[00:07:20] Priya: yes — export CSV / webhook to your eval infra. will include the prompt, generated outputs, delta metrics, and run metadata.

[00:07:36] Sofia: on the security piece, earlier you mentioned nothing leaves the VPC unless opted-in. how does that work for hosted vs private?

[00:07:44] Tom: for Redwood Private you run a customer-controlled control plane. logs and traces can be kept on-prem or forwarded to your SIEM. KMS/HSM integration is supported for key wrapping. for hosted, we offer a VPC peering option so the inference nodes sit in a customer VPC and only minimal control-plane metadata crosses the wire. We'll share the architecture diagram.

[00:08:10] Dana: timeline and pilot? we want to run a 2-week pilot with a 100k token budget and a focus on diagnostic prompts.

[00:08:18] Carlos: sounds good. typical pilot includes sandbox access, one Optimize engineer pairing session, and a fidelity sweep. we can do kickoff on 12/15 and run 12/16 - 12/29.

[00:08:31] Imran: pricing — how do you bill when adaptive fallback triggers FP8? is that charged as two requests or as the final variant?

[00:08:40] Tom: billing counts tokens consumed by the final execution path. re-rolls register as additional tokens consumed; our billing dashboard will break out adaptive-retries so you can see the incremental cost. We'll include a sample cost projection in the pilot doc.

[00:08:57] Dana: competitor question — we currently evaluate Anthropic endpoints and an in-house runtime for lower cost. why pick Redwood?

[00:09:05] Carlos: short answer: unified serving + policy-driven fallbacks + observability. you get precise SLO knobs, per-prompt policy routing, and the Optimize tooling to find the safe operating point. plus enterprise requirements (SAML, audit logs, VPC, KMS) baked in.

[00:09:22] Imran: re: observability, can we hook into our Prometheus and trace stack?

[00:09:26] Priya: yes — we expose Prom-compatible metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and per-request JSON artifacts through S3 or your own object store. we can also webhook eval results into your downstream pipelines.

[00:09:44] [short pause / murmur]

[00:09:55] Priya: circling back to precision details — INT8 quantization used here is asymmetric per-tensor with per-channel scales; FP8 is NVIDIA-style E4M3-ish representation in our runtime. we also run a mixed-precision path where embeddings use FP16, attention weights run FP8, and matmuls quantize to int8 on a case-by-case basis. this gives good sweet spots.

[00:10:20] Dana: does Redwood provide the quantization scripts or do we need to re-run them?

[00:10:26] Priya: we provide a toolkit in the sandbox. it's a small repro script — you can re-run with your private data locally if you want, and upload the profile to the console. the Optimize agent will then recommend thresholds and fallback rules based on your telemetry.

[00:10:45] Imran: curious about worst-case rollback — what if an FP8 regression occurs after rollout? how do we detect and rollback fast?

[00:10:53] Tom: we have an automatic rollback policy: if the rolling eval on production traffic exceeds a quality regression threshold for N minutes or M requests, the router flips to the stable variant and opens an incident. you can also configure a gradual canary with percentage ramping and an immediate fallback to last-known-good.

[00:11:12] Sofia: okay, for our security team we'll need the runbook text and the playbook for a rollback. can you share a copy?

[00:11:18] Carlos: yes, we'll add the rollback playbook to the pilot package.

[00:11:26] Dana: on the console, show cost/latency tradeoff charts for a sample split — say 90% INT8 / 10% FP8 vs 100% FP8.

[00:11:34] Priya: toggling the policy simulator — here are the projections. 90/10 mix reduces total compute cost by about 38% relative to 100% FP8 with only a 0.7 point drop in average entity F1; tail risk is bounded by the adaptive fallback.

[00:11:58] Imran: how accurate are these projections compared to real runs? what's the variance?

[00:12:03] Priya: projections use the actual kernel timings from the fleet and your sample prompt distribution. variance depends on workload burstiness and batch sizing; we include confidence bands in the sim output — usually +/- 6-12% for p95 in our tests.

[00:12:20] [crosstalk: agreement from Aurea attendees]

[00:12:30] Tom: also wanted to highlight telemetry sampling — we offer full-sample for pilot, but long term you might set a 2% sample with focused evaluation on tagged flows to reduce storage costs.

[00:12:45] Dana: good. one more question — how do model updates affect these profiles? we plan regular model refreshes.

[00:12:52] Priya: model updates create new profile versions. Optimize supports auto-compare between versions and will surface delta heatmaps. we recommend running a smoke fidelity sweep as part of your CI for model rollouts; the console can gate a rollout on passing thresholds.

[00:13:12] Imran: can we automate that gate in our CI pipeline?

[00:13:16] Priya: yes — we have an API endpoint for profile comparisons and a webhook that can return pass/fail to your CI.

[00:13:25] Sofia: networking logistics — do you require open egress for health checks?

[00:13:29] Tom: no open egress required for private. For hosted, there are control-plane callbacks, but you can restrict them to specific IP ranges, and we support VPC peering to avoid open internet paths.

[00:13:46] Dana: ok this is all useful. let's summarize next steps.

[00:13:50] Carlos: recap: 1) we'll spin up sandbox access + send pilot docs and SOC2/KMS architecture, 2) Priya will run the INT8/FP8 fidelity sweep on the 8 representative prompts you shared, 3) kickoff pilot 12/15, 2-week run, 4) Aurea provides 200 clinical prompts.

[00:14:12] Dana: confirmed, will send prompts by 12/10.

[00:14:18] Imran: one more micro ask — can we get a CSV export template of the fidelity sweep so we can pre-format our evals?

[00:14:25] Priya: yes i'll attach the template to the sandbox invite.

[00:14:31] Sofia: any legal/procurement blockers we should prep for?

[00:14:35] Carlos: standard pilot MSA and an NDA — we usually share a pilot addendum. we'll loop in legal after this call.

[00:14:44] [brief silence / typing]

[00:15:02] Priya: showing one last item — the fidelity drift monitor. after rollouts we continuously sample outputs and surface a drift score; if the score crosses a threshold we'll trigger alerting to Slack/email and start a rollback if configured.

[00:15:25] Dana: excellent. that gives us confidence.

[00:15:30] Carlos: cool, any final questions?

[00:15:34] Imran: just one logistics note — can the sandbox run in our preferred cloud region? latency matters for our EU clients.

[00:15:40] Carlos: yes, we'll provision in eu-west-1 for your pilot.

[00:15:45] Dana: great. thanks everyone.

[00:15:48] Carlos: thanks, we'll follow up with the deck, pilot docs, sandbox link, and SOC2/KMS artifacts. talk soon.

[00:15:55] [meeting ends / recording stops]

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hear of 'FP8' as 'F-P eight', 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K-V cash' in one spot, and small punctuation gaps.
